_readme: Content for the homepage app (index.html). render-hub.sh embeds it with repos.json; narration-clips.sh composes the spoken scripts from it.
beacon, virtues and gates are Distributed Virtue's canonical wording (dougdevitre/distributed-virtue, lib/beacon/). Change them there first, then here.
adoption: one entry per listed project in repos.json — who adopts it and the smallest useful pilot.

catalyst.name: Doug Devitre
catalyst.title: Community Development Catalyst
catalyst.welcome: I'm Doug Devitre. I build free, open tools for the places people fall through the cracks: courts, safety, housing, health, food and work. Then I help communities put them to use. Every project here starts the same way, with a person who is struggling, not with technology.
catalyst.distribute: Distributed virtue means character can spread the way information does. One person's skill becomes a whole community's capacity. Leaders start small: choose a virtue, choose a part of your community, and take one mindful step this week.
catalyst.blend: These pillars blend into one another. A family in crisis rarely needs just one door, so every project points to the ones it works beside.

beacon.title: Begin with humanity
beacon.prompt: Who is hurting, confused, excluded, or overwhelmed?

beacon.title: Examine the system
beacon.prompt: What are the institutions, resources, barriers, and information flows?

beacon.title: Augment people
beacon.prompt: Whose capacity does this increase, and how?

beacon.title: Create shared capacity
beacon.prompt: What reusable thing comes out of this — a guide, template, or workshop?

beacon.title: Open doors
beacon.prompt: Who cannot access this because of cost, literacy, language, disability, or distrust?

beacon.title: Never surrender judgment
beacon.prompt: Which decisions here stay with a named, accountable human?

virtues.name: Wisdom
virtues.question: What should we do?
virtues.practice: Before you decide, ask two people closest to the problem what they would do.

virtues.name: Courage
virtues.question: What am I standing for?
virtues.practice: Name one access gap out loud at your next meeting.

virtues.name: Justice
virtues.question: Who is being overlooked?
virtues.practice: Notice who is missing from the room, then invite one of them.

virtues.name: Compassion
virtues.question: Who needs to be heard?
virtues.practice: Spend ten minutes listening to someone you serve, without trying to fix anything.

virtues.name: Humility
virtues.question: What do I still need to learn?
virtues.practice: Ask a frontline worker what your organization gets wrong.

virtues.name: Temperance
virtues.question: Is this worth amplifying?
virtues.practice: Run your next public post through the Four Gates before you share it.

virtues.name: Honesty
virtues.question: Am I being transparent?
virtues.practice: Share one number your team is still working to improve.

virtues.name: Stewardship
virtues.question: What will I do with this power?
virtues.practice: Turn one thing you know into a guide someone else can use.

virtues.name: Hope
virtues.question: What better future can we build?
virtues.practice: Pick one tool on this page and try it this week.

access-to-justice.pilot: three transparency metrics in one circuit for one quarter

access-to-peace.adopter: mediators, parenting coordinators and family court services
access-to-peace.pilot: one program's co-parenting referrals for sixty days

access-to-safety.pilot: advocates preparing for safety-planning conversations in one office

access-to-services.adopter: social service agencies and health clinics
access-to-services.pilot: screening and referral at one intake desk

access-to-health.adopter: health navigators and community health centers

access-to-education.pilot: standards alignment for one grade band

access-to-housing.pilot: Fair Housing-safe market analysis in one office

access-to-food.pilot: the pantry map and events for one network

access-to-crew.pilot: two cleanup sessions drawn from 311 reports

access-to-care.pilot: one family's first living care plan

access-to-experts.pilot: one practitioner's methodology as a guided playbook
